title: Sprint 2 — Branching & Collaboration
description: Master branching, merging, conflict resolution, collaborative workflows, and advanced Git commands.

tickets.title: Ticket 1 — Branching Basics
tickets.description:
Create, switch, and delete branches.
Use a feature branch and merge via PR.
Rebase onto main.

tasks.title: Task 2.1.1 — Create, Switch & Delete Branches
tasks.description: Branching is a core part of Git workflows. Create a new branch named 'feature/test' and switch to it. Make a commit on this new branch, then switch back to the main branch. Finally, delete the feature branch you just created.

tasks.title: Task 2.1.2 — Feature Branch → Merge
tasks.description: Working collaboratively requires using Pull Requests. In the provided task repository, create a new feature branch and add a new item to the TODO list. Commit and push your branch to GitHub, open a Pull Request against the main branch, and successfully merge it.

tasks.title: Task 2.1.3 — git rebase onto Main
tasks.description: Your feature branch has fallen behind the main branch, and you want to maintain a linear project history. Update your feature branch by reapplying its commits on top of the latest main branch. After successfully doing so, update your remote feature branch (you may need to force your push).

tickets.title: Ticket 2 — Merge Conflicts
tickets.description:
Create and resolve a merge conflict manually.
Resolve a conflict using a merge tool.

tasks.title: Task 2.2.1 — Create & Resolve a Merge Conflict
tasks.description: Conflicts happen! You have two branches that modify the exact same line in a file. Merge one branch into the other, which will result in a conflict. Open the file, manually resolve the conflict markers so the final content is correct, and complete the merge with a new commit.

tasks.title: Task 2.2.2 — Resolve with a Merge Tool
tasks.description: For more complex conflicts, a visual merge tool is incredibly helpful. In this new conflict scenario, configure Git to use a merge tool (such as vimdiff or meld). Launch the tool to resolve the conflict, and then commit the successful resolution.

tickets.title: Ticket 3 — Git Workflows
tickets.description:
Practice GitHub Flow on a solo project.
Use Conventional Commits.
Tag a release.

tasks.title: Task 2.3.1 — GitHub Flow on a Solo Project
tasks.description: Practice the complete GitHub Flow end-to-end on a fresh repository. Create a feature branch, implement a small change, and push it. Open a Pull Request with a descriptive body, merge it into the main branch, and then clean up by deleting your feature branch.

tasks.title: Task 2.3.2 — Conventional Commits
tasks.description: Consistent commit messages make history much easier to read. Make 5 distinct commits to your repository, ensuring every single one strictly follows the Conventional Commits format (e.g., 'feat(auth): add login button'). Use a variety of commit types such as feat, fix, docs, or chore.

tasks.title: Task 2.3.3 — Tag a Release
tasks.description: Mark a significant milestone in your project by tagging a release. Create an annotated tag named 'v1.0.0' pointing to your latest commit, including a descriptive message for the tag. Once created, push this specific tag to your remote repository.

tickets.title: Ticket 4 — Advanced Git
tickets.description:
Cherry-pick a specific commit.
Practice reset, revert, and restore.
Write a pre-commit hook.

tasks.title: Task 2.4.1 — git cherry-pick a Specific Commit
tasks.description: Sometimes you need a specific fix from another branch without merging all of its changes. Identify the commit hash of the bug fix on the other branch, and apply only that specific commit to your current branch. Make sure the other branch remains untouched.

tasks.title: Task 2.4.2 — Reset, Revert & Restore (All Three)
tasks.description: Practice three different ways to undo changes. First, undo your very last commit while keeping its changes staged. Second, safely undo a commit that has already been pushed by creating a new inverse commit. Finally, completely discard all uncommitted changes in your current working directory, restoring the files to their last committed state.

tasks.title: Task 2.4.3 — Write a Pre-Commit Hook
tasks.description: Automate your quality checks! Write a pre-commit hook script that prevents anyone from committing a JavaScript file if it contains 'console.log' statements. The script should block the commit if it finds one, and allow it otherwise. Save your script in a 'hooks/' folder in the repository so it can be shared and evaluated.
